BYAN.text: Control is changing hands: Low Tuck Kwong sold 10.07 bn shares (40.15% → 9.95%) at Rp 2,588 to Haji Isam's Jhonlin Baratama, completed 8 Oct (≈ Rp 26.1 T for 30.25%). Press reports say the buyer funded it with a Bank Mandiri loan secured on pledged JARR and PGUN shares; a force majeure (14-24 Sep) has been lifted.

JARR.text: JARR's own shares were pledged to Bank Mandiri (7 Oct), reportedly to fund the Jhonlin group's purchase of 30.25% of Bayan (BYAN). The pledge is the risk: a forced sale is possible if that loan gets into trouble.

PTPP.text: Trading has been suspended since 5 Oct because PTPP missed a bond coupon or principal payment. It signed a Master Restructuring Agreement on 11 Sep, and Danantara wants it merged with ADHI this year; holders are locked in until the suspension is lifted.

ENRG.text: A deep-discount rights issue is under way: 1 new share for every 2 held at Rp 310 (13.3 bn shares, ≈ Rp 4.1 T), with exercise until 21 Oct. In the middle of it, ENRG signed an agreement with Nasdaq-listed HighPeak Energy (6 Oct), most likely what the money is for. Holders who do not exercise lose about a quarter of their value.

INET.text: Holder AKUN plans to sell 29.88% (6.69 bn shares) to CNI at Rp 300, about 21% above the price, for ≈ Rp 2.0 T, confirmed on 6 Oct but not yet signed. INET also paid Rp 280 B for 60% of Sarana Global Indonesia, and 2.3 bn warrants are still outstanding.

TPIA.text: Chandra Asri is turning into a regional conglomerate: it signed to buy Jardine's Cycle & Carriage car business in Singapore and Malaysia (debt-funded through Mizuho), and its Aster unit is buying into Changi Airport's fuel-hydrant operator. Price not disclosed; the question is how much new debt it takes on.

BRIS.text: Rights issue of up to 6.8 bn new shares (≈ 15% more shares) to fund financing growth; the vote is at the 6 Nov EGM and the price is not set yet. Whether the state controller takes up its full share in cash is the key question.

ULTJ.text: Transformational deal: an acquisition worth 178% of Ultrajaya's equity, of a target that earns 121% of ULTJ's profit, partly funded by a rights issue. Both are up for approval at the 27 Oct EGM.

VKTR.text: Rights issue of up to 15 bn shares at Rp 200 (12 new for every 35 held, trading 12-23 Oct), plus a non-binding term sheet for Danantara to invest in VKTR with Bakrie & Brothers as guarantor. State money would be a big vote of support; holders who skip the rights are diluted.

WIFI.text: Hashim Djojohadikusumo resigned as President Commissioner (29 Sep), and the 21 Oct EGM will add a new business line backed by a feasibility study. The politically linked chair leaving and a change of business at the same time: watch what WIFI becomes.

MGLV.text: Full makeover: MGLV sold its 13 household-goods subsidiaries and took over Nextier AI data-centre companies, lending them Rp 4 T. A rights issue of up to 285.7 M shares (≈ Rp 669 B) funds it. The value now rests entirely on a data-centre business with no track record.

SOFA.text: A furniture maker is becoming 'Solusi Environment Asia': the change of business was approved on 30 Sep, followed on 7 Oct by a material deal with an affiliated party done without a shareholder vote. Check the price and who benefits.

NAYZ.text: New controller Saiko (Singapore) bought 39.22% from Asia Intrainvesta, and a mandatory tender offer follows. NAYZ will also buy 75% of a company from Saiko itself: a classic backdoor-style injection that explains the speculative rally.

KETR.text: Sinar Mas's DSSA bought 35% of Ketrosden Triasmitra at Rp 523 after a voluntary tender offer, and is now the controller (28 Sep). A fiber builder joining the DSSA group.

IATA.text: IATA has left the MNC Group and is now part of the Karya Pacific Group (8 Oct), after sukuk holders waived the main-shareholder clause. A new owner usually brings a new plan or asset injections.

KDTN.text: A takeover by Ruby Mining (Hong Kong) of this small hotel company is progressing (8 Oct). That looks like a backdoor listing for a mining business, and a mandatory tender offer would follow.

MBSS.text: A new controller with shipbuilding links took over and made a mandatory tender offer (8 Sep); new directors are in. The tender price sets a floor for minorities.

DPUM.text: Unirama Group's PT Rama Indonesia (FMCG distribution) is the new controller, but it asked to postpone the mandatory tender offer.

VISI.text: New controller Harmoni Semesta Investama finished its tender offer (27 Aug). VISI is now changing its business into a holding company with a material transaction and a private placement (approved 30 Sep).

FUTR.text: An advertising company moving into drinking water: it is buying 51% of PT Dumai Tirta Persada from Adhi Karya for Rp 141 B (signed 30 Sep), after a change of owners behind its 45% controller.

PIPA.text: A PVC-pipe maker becoming a gas processor: Oxala signed a conditional deal (7 Sep) to buy PT Aztech Pandu Persada, driven by controller Morris Capital. The price and funding are the open questions.

MEJA.text: An interior-design company preparing to buy coal miner PT Trimata Coal Perkasa: an appraiser was appointed on 1 Oct. Watch who owns the target and whether new shares pay for it.

IRSX.text: Rights issue of up to 12.39 bn shares, about double the current count, approved with a new President Commissioner, DPR member Hana Hasanah Fadel Muhammad. Whoever takes up the rights may end up in control.

EPAC.text: Shutting its own flexible-packaging business on 31 Dec to move production into a new digital plant at a subsidiary, while planning a rights issue of up to 2 bn shares and a buyback.

AHAP.text: A forced rights issue of up to 3.5 bn shares (5 new for every 7 held) to meet OJK's minimum-equity rule for insurers. Heavy dilution for anyone who skips it.

BUVA.text: Rights issue of up to 6.15 bn new shares, with rights trading 19-30 Oct. Check the price and the standby buyer.

LAPD.text: Rights issue of up to 2 bn shares (EGM 20 Oct), partly payable in non-cash form, plus a director's resignation.

KOTA.text: A rights issue that appears to bring in other companies and land (Art Design Indonesia, Mandirinusa Grahaperkasa, appraised land at Gunung Anyar and Maja), voted at the 6 Oct EGM. Related-party asset injections need a close look at the appraisals.

GIAA.text: Garuda plans a third rights issue (PMHMETD III) after a management reshuffle at the 8 Oct EGM. In August its commercial director was temporarily dismissed by the BUMN agency.

APEX.text: Won a US$74.3 M (≈ Rp 1.3 T) offshore drilling contract from Pertamina Hulu Mahakam for 2+1 years, bigger than the company's market value. A private placement of 218 M shares at Rp 325 follows on 19 Oct.

AADI.text: Sold its stake in Australia's Kestrel coal mine (via ACL) in a deal worth about 20.7% of its equity (1 Oct). Cash for dividends, debt or a new acquisition.

PGAS.text: Lost a partial London arbitration award to Gunvor (LNG dispute) and must pay compensation. The amount is still unclear; IDX asked for details.

AUTO.text: Astra (ASII) is making a voluntary tender offer for up to 4.95% of AUTO at Rp 3,600, a floor while the offer runs.

MNCN.text: Binding deals with Republikorp's RMAB (14 Sep) for a strategic partnership and joint venture around the iNews group: new money and a politically connected partner for MNC's TV news.

TLKM.text: Phase 2 of separating wholesale fiber into Telkom Infrastruktur Indonesia is approved and signed (30 Sep), and TLKM now owns 100% of its data-centre company ahead of a partnership. Both set up possible stake sales that could unlock value.

BBCA.text: IDX asked BCA about a Tempo report denying that Haji Isam would acquire it (25 Sep). Nothing else beyond routine filings.

TOBA.text: The green pivot shows in the numbers: waste management and EVs are now 66.5% of revenue, gross profit more than doubled in 1H26, and TOBA got the first IDX 'Green Equity – Transition' label. It is still loss-making.

CUAN.text: Negotiating to take over listed PT Singaraja Putra (SINI), small for CUAN but a likely tender offer for SINI holders.

BUMI.text: Buying Australia's Loyal Metals for AUD 79 M (≈ Rp 1.0 T, corrected from Rp 3.2 T): a small step into metals.

KIJA.text: Bought 51% of industrial-estate developer Kawasan Industri Seafer for Rp 341 B (≈ 11% of its market cap), adding land bank.

ASII.text: Making a tender offer for up to 4.95% of its subsidiary AUTO at Rp 3,600, and paying an interim dividend while the buyback continues.

JPFA.text: Selling its animal-vaccine unit Vaksindo (and brands) to an affiliated party; the price and fairness opinion are the thing to check.

MDKA.text: A private placement (PMTHMETD IV) is still pending: IDX asked the price and MDKA cannot estimate it yet. It is also signing service contracts for the Pani gold mine.

EMAS.text: Pani gold mine financing and service contracts with group companies (material affiliated deals), plus an announcement on the Hong Kong exchange.

DKFT.text: Controller Jinsheng Mining keeps buying: 110 M shares at Rp 700, raising it from 63.79% to 65.74% (7 Oct).

HATM.text: PT Multi Sarana Nasional bought 640 M new shares at Rp 500 (Rp 320 B) in a private placement, raising it to 25.6%.

UVCR.text: Trimegah Sumber Mas sold 300 M shares at Rp 141 (31.2% → 16.2%), and a private placement is planned (EGM 27 Oct).

MSJA.text: IDX put MSJA on its high-shareholding-concentration list: very thin real float.

INDO.text: IDX put INDO on its high-shareholding-concentration list: very thin real float.

BDKR.text: IDX put BDKR on its high-shareholding-concentration list: very thin real float.

AMMN.text: A commissioner was named a suspect in the CNI nickel graft case (relating to before he joined), and Amman is reshaping its board. 1H26 results were strong with smelter cathode output ramping up.

ADRO.text: IDX asked about KPK raids after former Adaro executives were questioned; Adaro reports no impact.

SMRA.text: A KPK sting at the Bogor land office was reportedly linked to a Summarecon land title; SMRA did not deny a link.

PTBA.text: Took Rp 6 T of working-capital loans from BRI and Mandiri (23.7% of equity) against export proceeds that must stay onshore.

RAJA.text: Paying US$43.7 M for just 5% of PT Layar Nusantara Gas, implying ~US$870 M for the whole company.

BWPT.text: IDX asked about reports that Malaysia's Felda lost Rp 10.9 T on its BWPT stake and sought Prabowo's help: watch for a change in Felda's holding.

GOTO.text: EGM on 14 Oct to cancel shares bought back in 2024-25 and accept the resignation of vice-president director Catherine Hindra Sutjahyo.

BDMN.text: The merger with MUFG's Indonesian branch moves ahead: the new name will be Bank MUFG Danamon.

NISP.text: Completed buying OCBC Sekuritas and Great Eastern Life Indonesia from its parent group: now bank, broker and life insurer.

BBTN.text: Four directors were replaced at the 4 Sep EGM (13% voted against).

PSAB.text: The energy ministry approved the change of shareholders in its gold miner JRBM, a step in restructuring or selling the main asset.

MBMA.text: Share buyback plan, and IDX asked about a report it is considering depositary receipts in Hong Kong.

KOCI.text: Free float is only 12.8%, below IDX's minimum; it must explain how it will comply.

MOLI.text: IDX asked for its plan to meet the minimum free float.

RATU.text: Independent holders narrowly (51.9%) approved a private placement of up to 271.5 M shares (10%) to an investor not yet named.

HRTA.text: A gold-bar supply deal with Bank Mandiri, and a private placement vote on 16 Oct.

ARKO.text: Moving into solar for industrial estates (Batam, Bintan) and signed a Rp 691 B project loan.

CBRE.text: Rights issue under way while it answers a breach-of-contract lawsuit.

TRIN.text: The President Commissioner resigned (9 Oct); Artotel will run its Collins Boulevard hotel.

BIPP.text: A private placement of up to 503 M shares is stuck after an EGM missed quorum (re-run 16 Oct), and Victoria Investama sold down to 7.36%.

PART.text: Sales up 38%, preparing both a rights issue and a buyback.

DFAM.text: A bank is re-auctioning mortgaged property to recover a loan: a sign of financial stress.

RMKO.text: IDX asked why half-year results differ from the projections made at its IPO.

SMIL.text: Asked IDX for more time to answer questions about its financial report.

UNTD.text: IDX wants numbers behind a 68.8% jump in cost of goods sold: a margin squeeze.

SILO.text: Siloam is buying back the hospitals it leases: shareholders approved (22 Sep) taking over 14 First REIT property companies, Rp 6.9 T in stage one (≈28% of market cap) and up to Rp 14.5 T of loans and guarantees in total. Rp 3.47 T was already paid on 24 Sep; the rest of stage one is due by 1 Dec 2026, stage two at First REIT's option. Rent turns into owned assets plus debt.

PGUN.text: The controller Araya Agro Lestari pledged all 2.21 B of its shares (≈38%) to Bank Mandiri on 30 Sep for an affiliate's loan, and IDX asked (7 Oct) why the company said in August it had no plans. In August it denied knowing of the Bayan takeover rumour that lifted JARR, PGUN and FAST.

GRPM.text: A takeover is pending: the term sheet for a new controller to buy out PMUI (71%) and Agus Susanto was extended to 31 Dec 2026. A closing would normally trigger a tender offer to minority holders.

PMUI.text: PMUI itself is the target of the same pending takeover as its subsidiary GRPM (term sheet extended to 31 Dec 2026). It also bought 34% of a VinFast e-motorbike dealer (West Java).

VICI.text: Beauty Brands International sold its entire 25% stake (1.68 B shares at Rp 747, ≈Rp 1.25 T); three commissioners resigned in September and an EGM on 29 Oct will rebuild the board and change the business-purpose and directors'-powers articles. A BNI credit facility was signed.

ADMF.text: MUFG trimmed its direct stake from 18.9% to 14.4% (55.9 M shares at Rp 7,800, 29 Sep); Danamon keeps 75%. Otherwise routine: a commissioner resignation and a bond prospectus.

BBRM.text: A new AHTS vessel worth USD 12.1 M (≈23% of market cap, 32% of equity) was delivered and is ready to work, part-funded by a Rp 120 B Bank IBK loan; a separate PSV newbuild was cancelled at no cost. IDX is pressing it to reach the 15% minimum free float.

BNBA.text: Legal cases are pending against two directors, including the president director, and shareholders approved a full board overhaul on 10 Sep; new appointees await OJK approval.

CASH.text: Cashlez is changing course: shareholders approved new business activities (feasibility study by KJPP FDI&R) and a change in how its rights-issue money is used (EGM 8 Oct). What the new business earns is the open question.

DRMA.text: Dharma Polimetal formed a 49%-owned joint venture with China's Minth Group for EV battery housings and aluminium body parts (Rp 45 B paid-in). Small money now, a growth option.

DYAN.text: A subsidiary signed a conditional purchase of land and buildings from Dana Pensiun Kompas Gramedia (price in the filing). An IDX volatility query found nothing undisclosed.

FAST.text: A PKPU (debt-moratorium) petition against KFC Indonesia was withdrawn on 1 Oct; a director resigned and an EGM on 14 Oct changes the board.

FITT.text: Renamed Fortune Resources Investment and turned from a hotel company into a holding company (effective 4 Aug) under Jinlong Resources (79%): a shell waiting for assets.

ISEA.text: IDX asked why results lag the projections given at the IPO (letter of 10 Sep); the company replied in writing.

KKGI.text: Paid a Rp 20 cash dividend (Rp 97.5 B, ≈6.7% at Rp 298; ex 24 Sep, paid 15 Oct) and made Wimpi Salim president director.

LOPI.text: A cooperation agreement with China's CRRC Qiqihar on railway wagons and cranes (no value yet), and a third EGM call (19 Oct) to approve a private placement after two meetings lacked a quorum.

MAHA.text: Signed a coal-hauling contract with PT Ade Putra Tanrajeng running to 2030 (value not disclosed).

MERK.text: The P&G toll-manufacturing contract ends 31 Dec 2027, so the Pasar Rebo plant is being impaired; the site is valued at Rp 93 B (≈5.5% of market cap).

MPIX.text: IDX questioned results against the IPO projections; the company bought Rp 8 B of property with a 16% BPR loan. The controller sold 1.8% (59.997% → 58.237%).

SMKM.text: The long-stop date for buying PanAsia Aquaculture and LSO Organization was pushed to 30 Jun 2027 while the target restructures; the EGM and deal terms are still to come.

SKBM.text: A fire hit its Tangerang warehouse on 17 Sep; no casualties, operations continue, losses still being assessed.

SUNI.text: Won a USD 3.2 M Pertamina EP casing tender (≈3.4% of market cap) and put Rp 60 B into its pipe subsidiary; IDX asked about a loss-making unit.

PTSN.text: Took new Bank Mandiri lines of about USD 25 M (≈20% of market cap) for new projects; IDX asks for a plan to reach the 15% free float.

BPTR.text: IDX asks for a plan to reach the 15% minimum free float.

CITY.text: IDX asks for a plan to reach the 15% minimum free float.

PURI.text: Free float is below the 15% minimum; IDX asked for a plan (Bumi Kreasi Baru holds 77%).

BNII.text: Bought 51% of Etiqa Insurance Indonesia from the Maybank group for Rp 21.6 B (financial-conglomerate rules): small and intra-group.

IMJS.text: Set up PT Indomobil Global Ventura as a venture-financing vehicle for the Salim group ecosystem.
